title: Carbon-X DNA Model Matches GPT-6.1 Sol at 1,000x Lower Cost
summary:
Researchers have released an open 14B parameter model that integrates genomic data and natural language processing for biological analysis. Known as Carbon-X, the model performs within one point of GPT-6.1 Sol on DNA benchmarks while operating at more than 1,000 times lower inference cost. It outperforms all other open language models tested across five benchmarks, with its peak performance in completing DNA sequences and predicting mutation effects.

The model was developed by mid-training Qwen3-14B on 300B tokens of DNA, English and interleaved data using a hybrid tokenizer that encodes DNA with about 3 times fewer tokens than Byte Pair Encoding. Carbon-X is available under the Apache 2.0 license and can run locally on laptops via llama.cpp. When used as a specialist subagent, the model increases the score of Kimi K3 by 11.1 points.

selectedTweets.text:
Today we're releasing Carbon-X, a 14B model that brings DNA and natural language together for the first time 🧬

1. Beats every open language model we tested across DNA benchmarks. Within a point of GPT-6.1 Sol at >1,000× lower inference cost.

2. Mid-trained on 300B tokens of interleaved DNA and text, followed by SFT (without distillation!) and RL.

3. A new hybrid tokenizer encodes DNA using ~3× fewer tokens than BPE.

4. Gives other models a DNA specialist subagent: Kimi K3 gains 11.1 points when it consults Carbon-X.

5. Runs locally on a laptop with llama.cpp. Apache 2.0. Your DNA stays on your hardware.
